review_conclusions: Three retained bytearrays are 2048 bytes each. Thirty-two FP32 residue sums occupy bytes 0..127 of the output bank and are dead before BF16 output stores; no additional arithmetic H2048 input/weight/output bank.
Observer snapshots and per-row scalar diagnostics are explicitly host-only; callbacks receive immutable tuples and their return values never feed arithmetic.

Independent residue execution is interleaved but each block has sixteen ascending FP32 terms, each residue adds blocks 0,1,2,3, then ordered residue/lane reduction. Existing scalar operation/fault policy and final BF16 RNE remain intact.
Canonical schedule reads input twice and weight once per token: 12288 read bytes, 4096 write bytes, 192 read and 64 write requests of 64 bytes.

Inherited admission, exclusive scalar ownership, single outstanding request, accepted-response drain, abort/reset poison, held completion, final ACK and publication fence remain in use. Bounded M1 tests cover normal/fault paths and resource reuse.

Official reference executes the whole unchanged pinned Qwen3_5MoeRMSNorm class AST. Owner completes and publishes before official component/formula evaluation; neither reference supplies future inputs to owner arithmetic.
Original model and Transformers revision, current software-source identity and historical legacy/candidate associations are kept distinct; no inherited historical acceptance.

Original final materialized BF16 thresholds remain max_abs 0.03125 and mean_abs 0.005. FP32 internal official-stage comparisons are diagnostics; observed M16/M128 values are bit-exact. Native sqrt is absent and auxiliary native sum is labeled.
